start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep my computer's task taker running in my engine, taking the tasks given to it with my chosen AI". It switches on tool:take-given-tasks-on-this-computer's wake keep-taking-given-tasks on your computer with your settings (computer_name "Desk Computer (2)", chosen_ai "claude", tasks_store "my-tasks-connection") and a start-a-program grant for your AI program and work folder; from then on each task whose assignees name ai:take-open-work-desk-computer-2 is taken within a pass, done by the AI and finished from the result file it writes.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: the tasks are rows of the tasks table your own database already keeps, and the taker's own record is a row of its users table.
instructions: 1. Pick the AI program the taker starts (its path on this computer), the folder it keeps its settings in, and the one folder it may change files in.

2. Keep each of the AI's logins in your vault under a name of your own, and name them in logins and in settings.ai_auth (for example ai_auth.claude.claude_token_names). A run takes the first login that is not resting; a login that reaches its limit rests alone and the next one runs.

3. Switch the wake on with your input: wake:switch {tool: tool:take-given-tasks-on-this-computer, id: keep-taking-given-tasks, on: true, input: {settings, computer: {start-a-program: {...}}, logins}} (the worked example shows a whole input). A switch that leaves the computer name, the chosen AI, the tasks store or the grant's program or work folder empty is refused.

4. Give a task to the taker: its assignees name ai:take-open-work-<your computer name in lower case, words joined by dashes>. Read the task row: within a pass its status turns In progress with taken_by the taker, then Done with the result, or back to To do with the reason.
5. Read the taker's own row in your users table: live.seen_at moves at each pass. Switch the wake off to stop it; switching it on again keeps the input it was given.

6. To let this computer take tasks that name nobody, list the shapes it takes in settings.tasks.take_unassigned_when (none by default). Each shape maps a task field to the values it may hold, or to true (holds something) or false (holds nothing). For the waiting steps of your engine's workflow runs: [{"told_as.source": ["workflow-step-answered"], "for": ["anyone", "ai"], "asks.submit": true, "asks.checks": false}]. Every computer whose shapes fit a task may claim it and one wins, so a task never waits on a computer that is off. Its daily_cap and max_concurrent still bound how many it takes.

worked_examples.title: Switch the taker on for a computer whose tasks are kept in the person's own database
worked_examples.ask: Keep my computer's task taker running in my engine, taking the tasks given to it with my chosen AI
worked_examples.given: Two tasks whose assignees are ["ai:take-open-work-desk-computer-2"], status "To do", in the calendar_tasks table of the database my-tasks-connection opens.
worked_examples.hands_back: The switch answers {"switched": true}. Within a pass the first task reads status "In progress", taken_by "ai:take-open-work-desk-computer-2"; when the AI's run ends it reads status "Done" with the result the AI wrote, and the users row ai:take-open-work-desk-computer-2 shows live.seen_at at that pass.
